item.title: Afghan Men Quietly Resist Taliban Ban on Girls’ Education
item.description: The author is an Afghanistan-based female journalist, trained with Finnish support before the Taliban take-over. Her identity is withheld for security reasons

item.title: Human cost of violence in South Sudan ‘continues to grow’
item.description: Independent human rights investigators voiced deep concern over growing risks to both civilians and South Sudan’s political transition following their latest fact-finding mission to the world’s youngest nation – their 14th in a decade.

item.title: ‘An assault on humanity itself’: Guterres pays tribute to 9/11 victims, survivors and first responders
item.description: Twenty-five years ago, the heinous terrorist attacks of 11 September 2001 against the United States claimed thousands of lives and represented “an assault on humanity itself”, the UN chief said on Thursday.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Fresh attacks prompt emergency meeting on Yemen
item.description: On the heels of reported Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia on Tuesday and the capture of another key port by the militants on Yemen’s Red Sea coast – including the seizure of eight UN vehicles from a key aid hub there – the Security Council is meeting on Thursday at 3pm in New York to discuss the latest developments.

item.title: Ukraine: Drone attacks on Chornobyl are ‘gambling with the safety of millions of people’
item.description: A drone strike on the protective structure at the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant could have endangered the safety of millions of people, UN Development Programme (UNDP) Administrator Alexander De Croo told reporters via video link from Kyiv on Thursday.

item.title: UN climate chief warns political division is undermining fight against ‘economic security emergency’
item.description: The head of the UN's climate body has warned that treating global warming as a partisan issue is dangerously out of step with reality, as he set out a stark account of the economic toll climate change is already inflicting on Europe.

item.title: US Plans to Restrict Foreign Journalists Trigger Rising Protests
item.description: First, it was the mass deportations of undocumented aliens, then a crackdown on liberal-minded academics from prestigious US Universities, and now, restrictions on foreign journalists based in the US.
